title: The Illustrated Transformer
focus: The self-attention walkthrough (query, key and value vectors for one word, then the matrix form) and multi-head attention. Skim the encoder-decoder parts.

title: CS224N note: Self-Attention and Transformers (draft)
focus: The sequence of fixes: position representations, element-wise nonlinearities, causal masking. Then the full block with residuals and layer norm.

title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin
focus: Section 3.2 (scaled dot-product and multi-head attention, and the footnote on why scores are divided by sqrt(d_k)), Figure 2, and Table 1 (per-layer cost vs recurrence and convolution).

title: CS336 lecture 3: architectures and hyperparameters
focus: Pre-norm vs post-norm, RMSNorm, gated MLPs, RoPE, attention variants (GQA/MQA), and the hyperparameter ratios that recur across models.

title: The Transformer Family Version 2.0
focus: Positional encodings, long-context and efficient-attention variants. Read the section you need when a paper assumes it.

title: You could have designed state of the art positional encoding
focus: The progression from integer positions to sinusoids to rotations, and why a relative encoding should act on queries and keys rather than on the embeddings.

title: Rotary Embeddings: A Relative Revolution
focus: The derivation that rotating q and k makes their dot product depend only on relative position, and the implementation notes.

title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
authors: Su, Lu, Pan, Murtadha, Wen, Liu
focus: Section 3.2 (the 2D case, then the general block-diagonal rotation matrix) and the long-term-decay property of the rotated inner product.

title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Position Interpolation
focus: The bound showing attention scores can blow up at unseen positions, and why squeezing positions into the trained range plus a short fine-tune works.

title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
focus: The frequency-dependent view: interpolate low-frequency dimensions, leave high-frequency ones alone (NTK-by-parts), plus the attention temperature correction.

title: Let's build the GPT Tokenizer
focus: The BPE training loop, GPT-2/GPT-4 regex pre-tokenization, special tokens, and the closing list of tokenization-caused failures (spelling, arithmetic, non-English text, trailing spaces).

title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
focus: Section 3.2 and its Python listing (Algorithm 1). Implement it before reading anything else about BPE.

title: Language Model Tokenizers Introduce Unfairness Between Languages
focus: The tokenization-premium measurements across languages and their consequences: higher cost, higher latency and less usable context.

title: Making Deep Learning Go Brrrr From First Principles
focus: The three regimes (compute-bound, memory-bandwidth-bound, overhead-bound), operator fusion, and how to tell which regime a workload is in.

title: How to Think About GPUs (How to Scale Your Model)
authors: Jacob Austin, Sholto Douglas, Roy Frostig, Anselm Levskaya, Reiner Pope et al. (Google DeepMind)
focus: SMs, tensor cores, the memory hierarchy and NVLink/InfiniBand networking, each expressed as numbers for roofline estimates.

title: CS336 lecture 5: GPUs
focus: The execution model, the memory hierarchy, and why tiling, fusion and matmul shapes decide performance.

title: How to Optimize a CUDA Matmul Kernel for cuBLAS-like Performance: a Worklog
focus: The kernel-by-kernel progression (coalescing, shared-memory tiling, 1D and 2D block tiling, vectorised loads, warp tiling) and the throughput gained at each step.

title: Triton: an intermediate language and compiler for tiled neural network computations
focus: The core idea: program at the level of tiles and let the compiler handle scheduling and memory coalescing inside a tile. Then work through the official Triton tutorials (vector add, fused softmax, matmul).

title: Online normalizer calculation for softmax
focus: The one-pass algorithm that keeps a running maximum and rescales the running sum. Prove to yourself that it is exact.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
focus: Figure 1 (tiling across HBM and SRAM), Algorithm 1, and the IO-complexity analysis in Section 3.2. Then the backward pass with recomputation in the appendix.

title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
focus: Section 3: fewer non-matmul FLOPs, parallelising over sequence length, and splitting work across warps to cut shared-memory traffic.

title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
authors: Shah, Bikshandi, Zhang, Thakkar, Ramani, Dao
focus: Warp specialisation with asynchronous loads, overlapping softmax with the matmuls, and FP8 with incoherent processing to limit quantization error.

title: Transformer Inference Arithmetic
focus: KV cache bytes per token, why small-batch decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound, and the batch size where it turns compute-bound. Redo each number for Llama 3 8B.

title: Continuous batching from first principles
focus: The sections on the KV cache, chunked prefill and continuous batching: how requests are packed into one batch and scheduled.

title: All About Transformer Inference (How to Scale Your Model)
authors: Jacob Austin, Sholto Douglas, Roy Frostig, Anselm Levskaya, Reiner Pope et al. (Google DeepMind)
focus: Prefill vs decode rooflines, KV cache memory, the latency-throughput trade-off, and how to shard a model for serving.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
authors: Kwon, Li, Zhuang, Sheng, Zheng, Yu, Gonzalez, Zhang, Stoica
focus: Section 3 (KV cache waste: reservation, internal and external fragmentation) and Section 4 (block tables; copy-on-write sharing for parallel sampling and beam search).

title: Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference
authors: Pope, Douglas, Chowdhery, Devlin, Bradbury, Levskaya, Heek, Xiao, Agrawal, Dean
focus: The cost model for latency vs utilisation, the partitioning layouts for feedforward and attention layers, and why multiquery attention matters at long context.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
authors: Kaplan, McCandlish, Henighan, Brown, Chess, Child, Gray, Radford, Wu, Amodei
focus: The summary of results in Section 1 and Figure 1. Note which allocation conclusion Chinchilla later revised, and why (the learning-rate schedule was not matched to training length).

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
focus: Section 3: three estimation approaches (fixed model sizes, IsoFLOP profiles, a parametric loss fit L(N, D) = E + A/N^alpha + B/D^beta), and the result that parameters and tokens should grow in equal proportion with compute.

title: Chinchilla Scaling: A replication attempt
focus: How refitting the parametric approach on data reconstructed from the paper's figure gives estimates consistent with the other two approaches, and the implausibly narrow original confidence intervals.

title: CS336 lecture 9: scaling laws basics
focus: Data and model scaling, how to run small sweeps and extrapolate, and the pitfalls in fitting.

title: CS336 lecture 11: scaling details
focus: Case studies from published model reports, and hyperparameter transfer across scale (muP, batch size and learning-rate scaling).

title: The Ultra-Scale Playbook: Training LLMs on GPU Clusters
focus: The memory breakdown (weights, gradients, optimizer states, activations), then DP, ZeRO stages 1-3, TP, sequence and context parallelism, pipeline schedules and expert parallelism.

title: How to Parallelize a Transformer for Training (How to Scale Your Model)
authors: Jacob Austin, Sholto Douglas, Roy Frostig, Anselm Levskaya, Reiner Pope et al. (Google DeepMind)
focus: For DP, FSDP, TP and PP: the communication cost per step and the batch size or model size at which each becomes communication-bound.

title: CS336 lecture 7: parallelism basics
focus: Collective operations and their costs, then data, tensor and pipeline parallelism with the memory and communication each saves or adds.

title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
focus: Figure 1 and Section 5: the 2 + 2 + 12 bytes-per-parameter accounting, and how stages 1, 2 and 3 partition optimizer states, gradients and parameters.

title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
authors: Shoeybi, Patwary, Puri, LeGresley, Casper, Catanzaro
focus: Section 3 and Figure 3: column-parallel then row-parallel splits of the MLP and attention, so each block needs one all-reduce forward and one backward.

title: Mixed Precision Training
focus: Section 3: an FP32 master copy of weights, loss scaling (and the gradient histogram that motivates it), and FP32 accumulation.

title: FP8 Formats for Deep Learning
focus: The E4M3 and E5M2 encodings, why E4M3 gives up infinities to extend its range, and which tensors use which format (weights and activations vs gradients).

title: Microscaling Data Formats for Deep Learning
authors: Rouhani, Zhao, More, Hall et al.
focus: The block structure (32 elements share one power-of-two scale) and the experiments on which element formats hold up for inference and for training.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
focus: Section 3.3 (fine-grained tile- and block-wise scaling, and promoting partial sums to higher precision). Also Section 2 for multi-head latent attention and auxiliary-loss-free MoE load balancing.

title: Why Momentum Really Works
focus: The eigen-decomposition of the error on a quadratic, why the largest curvature limits the step size, and how momentum changes the convergence rate.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
focus: Algorithm 1 and Section 3 (bias correction). Skip the convergence analysis, which was later shown to be flawed.

title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
focus: Algorithm 2 (Adam with L2 regularisation vs decoupled weight decay, differences highlighted) and why L2 is not weight decay under adaptive methods.

title: Muon: An optimizer for hidden layers in neural networks
focus: The update (momentum, then approximate orthogonalisation with Newton-Schulz iterations), which parameters use Muon and which stay on AdamW, and the empirical results.

title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training
authors: Liu, Su, Yao et al. (Moonshot AI)
focus: The two changes: add weight decay, and rescale each matrix's update to match AdamW's update RMS so AdamW hyperparameters transfer.

title: Illustrating Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
authors: Nathan Lambert, Louis Castricato, Leandro von Werra, Alex Havrilla
focus: The three-stage diagram: pretrained model, reward model trained on comparisons, RL fine-tuning with a KL penalty to the reference model.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
focus: Figure 2 (SFT, reward model, PPO) and Section 3.5 (reward-model loss and the PPO-ptx objective). Note that outputs of the 1.3B tuned model were preferred to those of 175B GPT-3.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
authors: Rafailov, Sharma, Mitchell, Ermon, Manning, Finn
focus: Section 4: from the optimum of the KL-constrained objective to the DPO loss, and what the DPO gradient does. Then Section 5 on the reward reparameterisation.

title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
focus: Section 4 (GRPO: group-relative advantages instead of a value network, and the KL estimator) with its PPO-vs-GRPO diagram, and the unified view of SFT, rejection sampling, DPO, PPO and GRPO.

title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (the RLHF Book)
focus: Use as the reference text: reward models, regularisation, policy-gradient algorithms and direct alignment algorithms. The web version is at rlhfbook.com.

title: Understanding Reasoning LLMs
focus: The four approaches: inference-time scaling, pure RL, SFT plus RL, and SFT with distillation, and where each shows up in the R1 recipe.

title: Why We Think
focus: Parallel sampling vs sequential revision, RL for reasoning, and whether chains of thought are faithful.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
focus: R1-Zero (RL with rule-based rewards and no SFT; response length grows during training), the multi-stage R1 recipe, distillation into small models, and the unsuccessful attempts (process reward models, MCTS).

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
focus: How the best strategy (sequential revisions vs search against a process reward model) depends on question difficulty, and the compute-optimal allocation that is more than 4x more efficient than best-of-N.

title: CS336 lecture 16: RL from verifiable rewards
focus: Policy gradients to GRPO, and the published reasoning-model training recipes.

title: A Visual Guide to Quantization
focus: Number formats, symmetric vs asymmetric quantization, outliers and clipping, then post-training methods (GPTQ, GGUF) and quantization-aware training.

title: MIT 6.5940 TinyML and Efficient Deep Learning Computing (Fall 2024)
focus: The two quantization lectures: linear and k-means quantization, granularity, calibration, and quantization-aware training. Slides and recordings are linked from the course page.

title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
focus: The emergence of large-magnitude outlier features with scale, and mixed-precision decomposition (outlier dimensions in FP16, the rest in INT8).

title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
authors: Xiao, Lin, Seznec, Wu, Demouth, Han
focus: The per-channel smoothing factor that moves quantization difficulty from activations to weights, controlled by alpha, and the figure of activation vs weight magnitudes before and after.

title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
focus: The algorithm box: quantize columns in order and push each column's error onto the remaining columns using the inverse Hessian (via Cholesky), with lazy batched updates.

title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
focus: Speculative sampling and why it is exact, then the expected tokens per step and walltime improvement as functions of the acceptance rate alpha and draft length gamma.

title: Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling
authors: Chen, Borgeaud, Irving, Lespiau, Sifre, Jumper
focus: The modified rejection-sampling algorithm and its proof, and the measured speedups on a 70B model.

title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
authors: Cai, Li, Geng, Peng, Lee, Chen, Dao
focus: Extra decoding heads on the target model, and tree attention to verify many candidate continuations in one forward pass.

title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
focus: Drafting at the feature level (the second-to-top layer) instead of the token level, and why feeding in the sampled token resolves the uncertainty.

title: Mixture of Experts Explained
authors: Omar Sanseviero, Lewis Tunstall, Philipp Schmid, Sourab Mangrulkar, Younes Belkada, Pedro Cuenca
focus: Routing, load balancing and capacity factor, why MoEs are harder to fine-tune, and the serving trade-off (every expert must be in memory).

title: CS336 lecture 4: mixture of experts
focus: Routing functions, balancing losses, and the design choices of recent open MoE models.

title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
authors: Shazeer, Mirhoseini, Maziarz, Davis, Le, Hinton, Dean
focus: Noisy top-k gating and the auxiliary losses that keep experts balanced.

title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
focus: Top-1 routing, the capacity factor and dropped tokens, the auxiliary load-balancing loss, and selective precision for router stability.

title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
focus: Fine-grained expert segmentation plus always-active shared experts, and the evidence that experts specialise more.

title: The Annotated S4
focus: The continuous-time SSM, discretisation, and the recurrent vs convolutional views of the same model.

title: State Space Duality (Mamba-2), Part I: The Model
focus: How a selective SSM and a form of masked linear attention compute the same thing. Read part I (the model) and part III (the algorithm).

title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
focus: Sections 1-2: SSMs as both recurrences and convolutions, and why naive parameterisations fail. The structured-kernel math is optional.

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
focus: Section 3: why input-dependent (selective) parameters break the convolution trick, the hardware-aware parallel scan, and the synthetic tasks (selective copying, induction heads) that motivate it.

title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
focus: The semiseparable-matrix view, and the chunked SSD algorithm.

title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
authors: Olah, Cammarata, Schubert, Goh, Petrov, Carter
focus: The three claims (features, circuits, universality) and the curve-detector examples.

title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
focus: The residual stream as a communication channel, QK and OV circuits, and the zero-, one- and two-layer attention-only analyses that lead to induction heads.

title: Toy Models of Superposition
focus: The small ReLU toy model, the phase diagram of when features are stored in superposition, and feature geometry. The HTML version on transformer-circuits.pub is the canonical one.

title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
focus: How the sparse autoencoders are trained and evaluated, the feature examples, and feature steering.

title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model
focus: Case studies with attribution graphs (multi-step reasoning, planning ahead when writing poetry) and the stated limitations of the method.

title: Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations
focus: The formulas: standard error of an eval score, clustered standard errors for grouped questions, paired differences between two models, and sample-size planning.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
focus: Section 2.1: the unbiased pass@k estimator, why plugging the empirical pass rate into 1-(1-p)^k is biased, and the numerically stable implementation.

title: Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models
focus: The ways evaluations silently differ (prompt format, answer extraction, normalisation, few-shot selection) and the recommended practices.

title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
focus: The Bradley-Terry model, confidence intervals, and how model pairs are sampled.

title: The LLM Evaluation Guidebook
focus: The chapters on automatic benchmarks, human and model-as-judge evaluation, and troubleshooting. As of late 2025 the repository points to a maintained successor.

title: Building effective agents
focus: The workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelisation, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimiser) vs agents, and when not to build an agent.

title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
focus: The planning, memory and tool-use decomposition, with the key papers for each.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
focus: Figure 1 and Section 2: a retriever and generator trained end to end, and RAG-Sequence vs RAG-Token marginalisation.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
authors: Yao, Zhao, Yu, Du, Shafran, Narasimhan, Cao
focus: Figure 1 (reasoning-only vs acting-only vs interleaved traces) and the error analysis.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
authors: Liu, Lin, Hewitt, Paranjape, Bevilacqua, Petroni, Liang
focus: The U-shaped accuracy curve over the position of the relevant document, and what it implies for placing retrieved chunks.
